_readme: Companion notification lines. Placeholders: {city} {sunrise} {sunset} {daylight} {daysToSolstice} {minutesGained} {minutesLost} {mirrorDate}. 'darkening' = days getting shorter (summer solstice to winter solstice), 'brightening' = days getting longer. Moments: morning (around sunrise), beforeSunset (~30 min before), afterDark (evening). Milestones fire on their day instead of a normal line. Don't repeat a line within 14 days.

morning: Morning! The sun's up at {sunrise} in {city}. Go and grab a bit of it.
Rise and shine, slowly. Sunrise was {sunrise}. Coffee by a window counts.
{daylight} of daylight today. Spend a little of it outside if you can.
Good morning. Same light today as on {mirrorDate}. Nice to know it comes back.
Sun's up at {sunrise}. A ten minute walk now is worth an hour of scrolling later.
Morning, friend. {daysToSolstice} days until the light turns around. We've got this.
The sun showed up at {sunrise}. Let's be at least as reliable as the sun today.
beforeSunset: Enjoy the sun until {sunset}. Step outside for five, it's worth it.
Sunset in about half an hour ({sunset}). Look west if you can.
Last light of the day coming up at {sunset}. Catch it while it's here.
Golden hour, {city}. Phones up, or better still, phones down.
The sun clocks off at {sunset}. Give it a little wave goodbye.
afterDark: It may be getting dark, but light a candle and stay cosy, my friend. Soon enough the sun will be back.
Dark outside, warm inside. Blanket, tea, a good book. You're doing it right.
Long evening ahead. Perfect excuse for soup and an early night.
The dark is just the sun taking a breather. It's back at {sunrise} tomorrow.
{daysToSolstice} days to the shortest day. After that, every evening gets a little brighter.
Nights are long, but you're not alone in them. The whole hemisphere is lighting candles with you.
Cosy mode on. The light is coming back on {mirrorDate}, same as today, and more after that.
Hang in there. Winter is a season, not a forever.

morning: Morning! Sunrise at {sunrise}. The light is on its way back, you can feel it.
{minutesGained} more minutes of light than on the darkest day. Every one of them is yours.
Good morning. {daylight} of daylight today, and growing.
The sun beat you up again at {sunrise}. Let's make it a good one.
Morning, friend. Each day now is a little brighter than the last. Literally.
beforeSunset: Enjoy the sun until {sunset}. Later than last week, isn't it lovely?
Sunset at {sunset}. Remember when it was dark at four? Look at us now.
Still light out. Sunset isn't until {sunset}. Go stretch your legs.
Golden hour coming up. The evenings are coming back to us.
The sun's staying out later these days. {sunset} today.
afterDark: Dark again, but not for as long. The nights are shrinking now.
{minutesGained} minutes of extra light since the solstice. The tide has turned.
Another day closer to long summer evenings. Sleep well.
The darkest part of the year is behind you. Well done for getting through it.
Tomorrow will be a little brighter than today. That's a promise from the planet.

winterSolstice: Today is the shortest day. From tomorrow, the light starts coming back. We made it to the turning point.
Solstice! The darkest day of the year. Light a candle tonight, it's all uphill from here.
dayAfterWinterSolstice: The light has turned. Today is a few seconds longer than yesterday, and it only grows from here.
summerSolstice: The longest day of the year. {daylight} of light. Get outside and soak it up.
Midsummer! Stay up late, watch the sun go down at {sunset}. You earned it.
equinoxSpring: Spring equinox: day and night are equal today. From here, light wins.
equinoxAutumn: Autumn equinox: day and night are equal today. Time to stock up on candles and good books.
clocksBack: The clocks went back last night. Darker evenings ahead, but brighter mornings for now. Be gentle with yourself this week.
clocksForward: The clocks went forward! An hour less sleep, but sunset is suddenly at {sunset}. Worth it.
firstSunsetAfter5pm: Big day: sunset is after 5pm again ({sunset}). Light after work is back!
oneHourGained: One whole hour more light than on the darkest day. That's real progress, friend.
